Rashi on Makkot 5b:10:1.english: Beribbi says - That was his name.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:10:2.hebrew: הרגו - כלומר שלא הוזמו עד שנהרג הנדון על פיהם:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:10:2.english: They killed - That is, they were not found to be conspiring witnesses until the accused was executed on the basis of their testimony.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:15:1.hebrew: חייבי מלקיות מנלן - הברייתא אמתניתין קאי, דאמר אין עושין דין הזמה עד שיגמר הדין, ויליף לה מ״נפש בנפש״ דמשתעי בחייבי מיתות. חייבי מלקות מנלן? כלומר, העידוהו שחייב מלקות והוזמו, מנלן דאין לוקין אלא אם כן נגמר הדין תחלה על פיהם:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:15:1.english: Those liable to lashes, from where [do we derive this]? - [The baraita] refers to the Mishnah, which says that we do not apply the law of conspiring witnesses until the verdict has been completed, and [the baraita] derives this from "a life for a life," which speaks of those liable to death. Those liable to lashes, from where [do we derive it]? That is, if [witnesses] testified against him that he is liable to lashes and they were [then] found to be conspiring witnesses, from where do we know that [the witnesses] are not flogged unless the verdict was first completed on the basis of their testimony?

Rashi on Makkot 5b:16:1.hebrew: חייבי גליות מנלן - אם העידוהו שחייב לגלות, והוזמו, ותנן במתניתין סופג את הארבעים — מנלן שאינו סופג אלא עד שיגמר הדין? דהני, הואיל ולאו מדין "כאשר זמם" קא מתרבו, לא אתי מלקות דידהו מגזירה שוה דרשע רשע, דמההוא לא ילפינן אלא עדים זוממין שהרשיעו הנידון ללקות (או למיתה), דהאי "רשע רשע" בנידונין כתיב:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:16:1.english: Those liable to exile, from where do we know [this]? - [If witnesses] testified about him that he is liable to be exiled, and they were found to be conspiring witnesses — and we learned in the Mishnah that he receives the forty lashes — from where do we know [that they receive lashes only] once the judgment has been concluded? For these [witnesses], since they are included [in punishment] not through the law of “as he conspired,” their lashes cannot come from the verbal analogy of “wicked person” – “wicked person,” for from that [analogy] we derive only [the case of] conspiring witnesses who caused the one who was judged to be found guilty of lashes (or death), since this “wicked person” – “wicked person” is written regarding those who are judged.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:17:1.hebrew: אראה בנחמה - לא אראה בנחמה. וגמרא הפכו לברכה. פ"א אראה בנחמה, נשבע: ימותו בניו, ואראה בנחמתן:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:17:1.english: I will see the consolation - [Meaning,] I will not see the consolation; and the Gemara turned it into a blessing [i.e., phrased it positively]. Another explanation: "I will see the consolation" — he swore: May his sons die, and may I see their consolation.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:17:2.hebrew: אם לא הרגתי עד זומם - שלא הוזם אלא אחד מהם, והרגתיו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:17:2.english: If I did not kill a conspiring witness - [I swear that] only one of them was proven to be conspiring, and I killed him.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:18:1.hebrew: שהרי אמרו חכמים כו' - מתניתין היא, מה שנאמר: שנים אין נהרגין עד שיזומו שניהם, דכתיב "והנה עד שקר העד". ואמר מר (סוטה דף ב:): כל מקום שנאמר "עד", הרי כאן שנים, עד שיפרוט לך הכתוב אחד:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:18:1.english: For the Sages said, etc. - It is a mishnah, [referring to] what [it says]: Two [witnesses] are not executed unless both of them are rendered conspiring, as it is written (Deuteronomy 19:18), "and behold, the witness is a false witness." And the Master said (Sotah 2b): Anywhere that it says "witness," there are two here, until the verse specifies one for you.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:19:1.hebrew: אלא בפני שמעון - שאם יטעה, יורהו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:19:1.english: Only before Shimon - So that if he errs, he [Shimon] will instruct him.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:19:2.hebrew: כסבורין - הכל, בלילה או ביום, ואינן רואין אותו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:19:2.english: They thought - Everyone, at night or by day, and they do not see him.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:1:1.hebrew: שקדמו והרגו - את הכת הראשונה, קודם שתבוא כת שניה:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:1:1.english: That they preceded and executed - the first set [of witnesses], before the second set came.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:22:1.hebrew: מה שנים אין נהרגין עד שיזומו שניהם - כדפרישית לעיל:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:22:1.english: Just as two are not killed unless both of them are found to be conspiring witnesses - As I explained above.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:23:1.hebrew: ר' עקיבא אומר לא בא השלישי כו' - לא הוצרך ללמדנו זאת, דממילא ידעינן ששנים מזימין את השלשה, שהרי השנים כשרים לכל עדיות; וממילא ידעינן שאין זוממין עד שיזומו כולם, שהרי כולם כאחד נעשו עדים, וקרא כתיב "והנה עד שקר העד". ולא בא אלא להחמיר עליו, שלא תאמר: הואיל ובלאו הוא היתה העדות מתקיימת, לא יעשו בו דין הזמה — לימדך הכתוב שאף הוא מן המקיימי דבר:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:23:1.english: Rabbi Akiva says: The third [witness] did not come, etc. - It was not necessary to teach us this, for we know it anyway: that two [witnesses] can render the three conspiring, since the two are valid for all testimonies; and we also know that [witnesses] are not deemed conspiring until all of them are rendered conspiring, since all of them were made witnesses as one, and the verse states, "and behold, the witness is a false witness." And [the third] came only to be stringent with him — so that you should not say: Since the testimony would have stood even without him, they should not apply the law of conspiring witnesses to him — the verse taught you that he too is among those who establish the matter.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:24:1.hebrew: על אחת כמה וכמה כו' - שמצינו מדה הטובה מרובה ממדת פורענות: במדה טובה הוא אומר (שמות ל״ד:ז׳) נוצר חסד לאלפים, במדת פורענות הוא אומר (שם) על שלשים ועל רבעים:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:24:1.english: All the more so, etc. - For we find that the measure of goodness is greater than the measure of punishment: regarding the measure of goodness, it says (Exodus 34:7) "Preserving kindness for thousands," [while] regarding the measure of punishment, it says (ibid.) "upon the third and upon the fourth [generations]."

Rashi on Makkot 5b:2:1.hebrew: מאי דהוה הוה - ולמה לי למיתני? אלא כת ראשונה:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:2:1.english: What was, was - And why do I need the Mishnah to teach this? Rather, it must be referring to the first set of witnesses.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:2:2.english: Alone - This implies that there is another [set of witnesses].

Rashi on Makkot 5b:3:1.hebrew: אישתקור - הכחישו זה את זה בדרישות של בית דין, כשבדקום:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:3:1.english: Were proven to be liars - They contradicted one another in the examinations of the court when [the court] examined them.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:3:2.hebrew: הוחזקה זו - להביא עדי שקר, ולא נקבל עוד עדות אחרת:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:3:2.english: This [woman] has been presumed - [She has been presumed] to bring false witnesses, and we should not accept any further testimony [from her].

Rashi on Makkot 5b:3:3.hebrew: אם היא הוחזקה - שהיא הוחזקה לחזר אחריהם, הרי כל ישראל מי הוחזקו לשמוע לה שתחזיק את האחרים כשקרים?:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:3:3.english: If she has been presumed - to seek out [false witnesses], has all of Israel been presumed [likewise] to listen to her, that she should establish the others as liars?

Rashi on Makkot 5b:4:2.hebrew: הדר חזייה לר' אלעזר בישות - החזיר ריש לקיש את פניו ונסתכל ברבי אלעזר בפנים זועפות, שהבין ריש לקיש ששמע ר' אלעזר דבר זה מפי רבי יוחנן, וכשאמרה לו לא אמרה בשמו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:4:2.english: He turned and looked at Rabbi Elazar angrily - Reish Lakish turned his face and looked at Rabbi Elazar with an angry countenance, for Reish Lakish understood that Rabbi Elazar had heard this matter from the mouth of Rabbi Yochanan, and when he said it to him, he did not say it in his name.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:5:1.hebrew: דאמר כר' יהודה - במתניתין: איסטטית היא זו, והוחזקה להזים:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:5:1.english: Who said [it] like Rabbi Yehuda - In the Mishnah, [Rabbi Yehuda said]: This woman is a stateit (a flatterer), and she has been established as a one who testifies falsely.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:6:1.hebrew: דליכא דקא מהדר - שאין אדם מחזר אחריהם לשכרם ולהרגילם תמיד לבוא לבית דין ולהזים את כל הבאים:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:6:1.english: Where there is no one who is seeking - For no person seeks them out to hire them and to accustom them always to come to the court and to refute all those who come.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:6:2.hebrew: דקא מהדרא - לבקש ולשכור עדי שקר:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:6:2.english: That she is seeking - To search for and hire false witnesses.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:7:1.hebrew: הני ידעי בסהדותא - אלו האחרונים ידעי בעדותה של זו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:7:1.english: These know the testimony - These last ones know the testimony of this one.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:8:1.hebrew: עד שיגמר הדין - אלא אם כן נגמר תחלה הדין של הנדון ליהרג, ואחר כך הוזמו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:8:1.english: Until the verdict is concluded - [They are executed] only if the verdict of the one condemned to be killed was first concluded, and afterward they were rendered conspiring witnesses.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:8:2.hebrew: נפש בנפש - בעדים זוממין כתיב: "לא תחוס עינך, נפש בנפש":
Rashi on Makkot 5b:8:2.english: A life for a life - It is written with regard to conspiring witnesses: "Your eye shall not pity; a life for a life."

Rashi on Makkot 5b:9:1.hebrew: לעשות לאחיו - משמע שהרי אחיו עדיין קיים:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:9:1.english: To do to his brother - It implies that his brother is still alive.

Rashi on Makkot 5b:9:2.hebrew: יכול משקבלו עדותן - ובאה להם הזמה מיד, קודם גמר דינו של נדון — יהרגו:
Rashi on Makkot 5b:9:2.english: One might have thought [that] from the moment they accepted their testimony - and the conspiracy [of the witnesses] came upon them immediately, before the verdict of the accused was concluded — they would be executed.

Tosafot on Makkot 5b:15:1.hebrew: חייבי מלקיות מנין - פי' מנין דאין לוקין עד שיגמר הדין על פיהם. וא"ת, ואמאי לא בעי נמי כן "חייבי ממון מנין" דאין משלמין ממון עד שיגמר דינו על פיהם? וי"ל, דכמו דבדיני נפשות דרשינן עד שיגמר דינו מקרא דנפש בנפש דכתיב בעדים זוממין, כמו כן כתיב ממון בעדים זוממין, דכתיב "יד ליד לא ינקה", דמפקי מיניה (כתובות דף לב:) דממונא משלמין, ודרשינן מיניה עד שיגמר הדין:
Tosafot on Makkot 5b:15:1.english: Those liable to lashes, from where [is it derived]? - Explanation: From where is it derived that one does not administer lashes until the judgment is concluded on the basis of [the witnesses'] testimony? And if you say: Why does [the baraita] not likewise ask, "Those liable to pay money, from where [is it derived]?" — that one does not make [the defendant] pay money until his judgment is concluded on the basis of their testimony? One can answer: Just as in capital cases we derive that the judgment must be concluded from the verse "a life for a life," which is written regarding conspiring witnesses, so too money is stated regarding conspiring witnesses, as it is written: "Hand for hand shall not go unpunished," from which they derive (Ketubot 32b) that [conspiring witnesses] pay money, and from it we derive that the judgment must be concluded.

Tosafot on Makkot 5b:16:1.hebrew: חייבי גליות מנין - פירוש: מנין דאין לוקין עד שיגמר דינו. וקשיא, דהא כשהעידו אחייבי גליות הרי הן חייבי מלקות, וחייבי מלקות כבר גמרנו מ"רשע" "רשע". ופ"ה דמההיא לא ילפינן אלא עדים הזוממין שהרשיעו הנדון ללקות או למיתה, דהאי קרא דרשע רשע בנידונין כתיב, אבל כשהרשיעו הנדון לגלות לא גמרינן:
Tosafot on Makkot 5b:16:1.english: Those liable to exile — from where [is it derived]? - Explanation: From where [do we derive] that one does not administer lashes until the judgment has been finalized? And this is difficult, for when [witnesses] testified against those liable to exile, [if they are found to be conspiring witnesses] they themselves are liable to lashes, and as for those liable to lashes, we have already derived [the law] from the verbal analogy of "wicked" "wicked." And Rashi explains that from that [verbal analogy] we derive only [the case of] conspiring witnesses who made the one judged out to be wicked [and liable] to lashes or to death, for that verse of "wicked" "wicked" is written with regard to those who are being judged [for lashes or death]. But when they made the one judged out to be wicked [and liable] to exile, we have not derived [that law].

Tosafot on Makkot 5b:1:1.hebrew: איסטטית היא - ברב אלפס פי' לשון סטים (שבת דף פט:):
Tosafot on Makkot 5b:1:1.english: "It is an istatit" - In the Rav Alfas [i.e., the Rif], it is explained as an expression of setim [i.e., deviation or wandering] (Shabbat 89b):

Tosafot on Makkot 5b:21:1.hebrew: אף השנים מזימין הג' ומנין אפי' הן מאה ת"ל עדים - תימה: אימא דעדים אתא אפי' לארבעה, ונמצא אחד קרוב או פסול יותר מן הג' דכתיבי בקרא; אבל טפי מארבעה לא. וי"ל: כיון שכת אחת מזמת שתי כתות, הוא הדין מאה:
Tosafot on Makkot 5b:21:1.english: "So too, the two can render the three conspiring witnesses; and from where [do we know this even if there are] one hundred? The verse states: 'witnesses'" - It is puzzling: Say that the word "witnesses" comes to include even four, such that if one of them is found to be a relative or disqualified, [the testimony is invalidated] — more than the three written in the verse; but not more than four. And one can answer: Since one group can render two groups conspiring witnesses, the same law applies to one hundred.
